correctness.rationale: For 2<x<3, terminal N is exactly 1 plus an endpoint-placement Bernoulli. Its success probability is the charge-weighted beta-tail mixture qR+hM+kA and is strictly increasing from zero to one, proving unique variance maximum 1/4. Beta weak limits yield the positive-gap regime. At exponentially small normalized gap e=exp(-s/t), both attractive shapes contribute e^{-s} while the repulsive shape vanishes, giving the exponential regime. For e=c sqrt(t log(1/t)) at critical weight w=1/2, P-1/2 divided by t log(1/t) tends to 3c^2-1/4, giving exact c=1/sqrt(12) by monotone bracketing. An actual standalone numerical checker independently rebuilt 16 charge channels, verified beta-probability identities and asymptotic parameter families, and compared sampling; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: The finite-shell terminal count has a natural maximal-uncertainty length at which one and two adsorbed segments are equally likely. Its scale is not a cosmetic parameter optimization: crossing a sharp charge-composition threshold changes it from exponentially small to logarithmically corrected algebraic to macroscopic, with a universal critical coefficient. This predicts exactly when fixed-grid sampling of near-threshold jamming fluctuations can miss their peak and distinguishes endpoint localization from regular deposition channels. It makes no exaggerated global thermodynamic claim.
